original_title: Musk's Starlink Positioned to Seize $2.4B FAA Contract He Helped Undermine

existing.title: Musk's Starlink Positioned to Seize $2.4B FAA Contract He Helped Undermine
existing.description_short: Musk's Starlink Positioned to Seize $2.4B FAA Contract He Helped Undermine
existing.description_long: In late February 2025, the Washington Post, AP, and Bloomberg reported that the FAA was on the cusp of canceling a $2.4 billion contract awarded to Verizon in 2023 for upgrading the nation's air traffic control communications backbone, and handing the work instead to Elon Musk's Starlink (owned by SpaceX). The existing Verizon FENS contract was designed to connect 4,600 FAA sites over 15 years. A SpaceX-led team embedded inside the FAA — several members of which had been given FAA email addresses — was the team recommending the switch. Senior FAA career officials refused to sign paperwork authorizing the contract change, so DOGE sought support from Trump-appointed acting FAA administrator Chris Rocheleau. Musk had publicly posted on X that the Verizon system was not working and posed catastrophic failure risk within single digit months — claims experts said were unsupported. The FAA itself regulated SpaceX for rocket launches and had pending civil penalty proceedings against the company. Ethics experts at Georgetown and UC Santa Clara said the arrangement was an extraordinary conflict of interest. Musk's DOGE role gave him access to FAA staffing decisions, budget cuts, and contract processes at the very agency that oversaw his private company's launches.

original_title: Trump Guts Wildfire Prevention Funding Weeks After Los Angeles Burns

existing.title: Trump Guts Wildfire Prevention Funding Weeks After Los Angeles Burns
existing.description_short: Trump Guts Wildfire Prevention Funding Weeks After Los Angeles Burns
existing.description_long: In the weeks immediately following the January 2025 Los Angeles wildfires — expected to be the costliest in U.S. history with losses potentially reaching $35 billion — the Trump administration froze wildfire prevention funding, fired thousands of firefighting-adjacent personnel, and halted seasonal firefighter hiring across the country. By February 13-14, 2025, reports confirmed that the administration had frozen all remaining funds from the $3 billion in wildfire mitigation money appropriated through the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law and Inflation Reduction Act, canceling contracts with non-profits like the Oregon-based Lomakatsi Restoration Project. On February 15, 2025, the New York Times reported that 3,400 U.S. Forest Service employees — roughly 10% of the agency's workforce — had been terminated, eliminating trail crews, fuel-reduction specialists, and training instructors who form the backbone of wildfire preparedness. A planned 151,434-acre prescribed burn in Everglades National Park was canceled; training programs for forest firefighters were scrapped mid-season; and seasonal hiring stalled just as fire season approached. Federal firefighters told ProPublica that it's always cheaper to do a prescribed burn than to fight an escaped wildfire, while the annual area burned by U.S. wildfires over the past decade was already 43% larger than the historical average tracked since 1983.

original_title: Auto Industry Hit: GM Profits Drop 35%, Ford Takes $800M Tariff Loss

existing.title: Auto Industry Hit: GM Profits Drop 35%, Ford Takes $800M Tariff Loss
existing.description_short: Auto Industry Hit: GM Profits Drop 35%, Ford Takes $800M Tariff Loss
existing.description_long: Trump's 25% tariff on all imported finished vehicles and parts, imposed in early April 2025, devastated the North American auto industry. General Motors reported a 35% drop in second-quarter 2025 profits, including a $1.1 billion direct tariff hit, and warned its full-year tariff impact could reach $4–$5 billion. Ford took an $800 million tariff hit in Q2 2025 alone. Stellantis estimated tariff costs of up to 1.5 billion euros for 2025. S&P Global Mobility projected that a third of North American vehicle production could be cut just in the first weeks after the tariffs — roughly 20,000 units per day. Anderson Economic Group calculated tariff-driven cost increases of $6,200 for small cars, $8,000 for pickup trucks, $9,000 for full-size SUVs, and up to $12,200 for electric vehicles with Chinese battery components. GM announced cutting the Oshawa, Ontario plant from three shifts to two, laying off 750 workers. Windsor's Stellantis plant alternated between reduced schedules and full shutdowns. Ford CEO Jim Farley told investors: What we're seeing is a lot of cost and a lot of chaos. Despite absorbing billions in losses, automakers held prices stable through mid-2025 to avoid customer backlash, meaning the full consumer price impact had not yet materialized.

existing.description_long: Beginning January 20, 2025, DOGE operatives were granted access to the Treasury Department's Bureau of the Fiscal Service payment systems — systems that disbursed $5.45 trillion in fiscal year 2024 — without signing security rules of behavior, without completing required IT security training, and without proper background screening. Treasury's own threat intelligence team circulated an internal email calling the access the single greatest insider threat risk the Bureau of the Fiscal Service has ever faced, recommending DOGE staff be placed under insider-threat monitoring immediately. A GAO report released April 2026 confirmed a DOGE employee had been inadvertently granted write/modify access and that unencrypted payment data was improperly transmitted outside the bureau. Separately, NPR reported in April 2025 that two DOGE staffers — 23-year-old former SpaceX intern Luke Farritor and venture capitalist Adam Ramada — were given accounts on classified nuclear weapons networks at the Department of Energy including the NNSA Enterprise Secure Network and SIPRNet, neither having prior security clearances or nuclear experience. A login attempt from a Russian IP address using newly created DOGE credentials was detected at the National Labor Relations Board, raising alarm that the unprecedented access to federal classified infrastructure may have extended to hostile foreign actors.

In July 2025, Gabbard declassified and publicly released a minimally-redacted 2017 House Intelligence Committee Republican report on Russia's 2016 election interference over the objections of CIA officials, who warned it exposed sensitive human sources and NSA signals intercepts used to monitor the Kremlin. Former CIA officer Susan Miller said publicly that Gabbard and the White House were lying about the Russia interference assessment, while Putin's government watched American intelligence infrastructure tear itself apart from within.

existing.description_short: Trump Systematically Fabricates Economic Statistics Across 2025 Rally Speeches
existing.description_long: Throughout 2025, President Trump delivered a pattern of provably false economic statistics, documented across multiple FactCheck.org and AP News analyses. At a December 9 Pennsylvania rally, Trump falsely claimed he had inherited the worst inflation in the history of our country — in fact the worst post-WWI inflation occurred after World War I — and that inflation had stopped, when BLS showed 3% inflation for the 12 months ending September 2025. He claimed gasoline was at $1.99 in three or four states when no statewide average was below $2.37. He claimed 4,000 new Pennsylvania manufacturing jobs when national manufacturing employment was down 49,000. In March 2025, Trump falsely claimed he was presiding over a brand-new domestic manufacturing boom after major collapse under Biden, when manufacturing jobs rose by 610,000 under Biden's full term. He cherry-picked Biden's final year loss of 111,000 manufacturing jobs while ignoring the four-year net gain. In June 2025, Trump claimed $88 billion in tariffs in two months when the accurate figure spanned 8 months and included Biden's tenure. AP News concluded Trump's glowing account of progress under his watch was out of tune with the experience of price-squeezed Americans and the story told by some of his government's own statistics.

existing.description_long: EO 14248 represented the most sweeping assertion of presidential authority over elections since the founding, claiming power to direct the independent Election Assistance Commission, require documentary proof of citizenship on the federal voter registration form, impose new voting machine certification standards that would force 39 states to replace equipment at a cost of billions of dollars, and deploy DOGE as a roving investigator of state voter rolls. Courts across the country issued injunctions blocking major provisions; in April 2025, a DC district court found the president's authority was at its lowest ebb because the order contradicted the manifest will of Congress; in June 2025, a Boston court blocked five additional provisions on behalf of 19 states. A Congressional Research Service analysis published September 16, 2025, concluded the order purports to change the rules of federal elections in ways the president lacked constitutional authority to do. The Brennan Center's August 2025 report documented how the EO was being combined with DOJ task forces, DOGE database access, and personnel purges to construct a comprehensive federal apparatus for controlling election outcomes.

existing.description_long: On September 20, 2025, Trump posted a lengthy message on Truth Social that had been intended as a private direct message to Attorney General Pam Bondi — but was accidentally posted publicly. In it, Trump addressed Bondi directly as Pam and demanded action against his political adversaries: What about Comey, Adam Shifty Schiff, Leticia??? They're all guilty as hell, but nothing is going to be done. We can't delay any longer, it's killing our reputation and credibility. He concluded with: They impeached me twice, and indicted me (5 times!), OVER NOTHING. JUSTICE MUST BE SERVED, NOW!!! According to NBC News, Trump was surprised to discover he had published the message publicly and tried to shrug it off. The post directly contradicted Trump's repeated public claims that he did not involve himself in DOJ charging decisions. In the weeks following the post, both Comey and James were indicted. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer called the conduct the path to a dictatorship. Senator Adam Schiff, who was named in the post, said Trump was using the DOJ to go after his political enemies and protect his political friends. Trump later told reporters he had nothing to do with the Comey case, directly contradicting the documentary record of his own post.

original_title: Trump Calls for Impeachment of Judge Boasberg Over Deportation Ruling

existing.title: Trump Calls for Impeachment of Judge Boasberg Over Deportation Ruling
existing.description_short: Trump Calls for Impeachment of Judge Boasberg Over Deportation Ruling
existing.description_long: On March 18, 2025, Trump publicly called for the impeachment of U.S. District Chief Judge James Boasberg on Truth Social, calling him a Radical Left Lunatic of a Judge, a troublemaker and agitator and declaring This judge should be IMPEACHED!!! The attack came after Boasberg issued a temporary restraining order on March 15 halting Trump's use of the 1798 Alien Enemies Act to rapidly deport hundreds of alleged Venezuelan gang members without due process. Boasberg ordered deportation flights that were already airborne to turn back; the administration did not comply. In a rare rebuke, Chief Justice John Roberts issued a written public statement saying that impeachment is not an appropriate response to disagreements concerning a judicial decision. Trump continued his attacks undeterred and began fundraising off the impeachment call. Elon Musk simultaneously posted repeatedly on X calling for Republican lawmakers to impeach Boasberg. The administration stonewalled Boasberg's demands for information about the flights, with a DOJ attorney repeatedly telling the judge he was not authorized to provide details — an extraordinary rebuff of a sitting federal judge. A contempt inquiry was opened and then paused for appeals. In July 2026, Republican Senator Eric Schmitt introduced legislation named the BOASBERG Act in a further attempt to curtail the judge's authority.

original_title: DOJ Fires 12+ Prosecutors Who Investigated Trump

existing.title: DOJ Fires 12+ Prosecutors Who Investigated Trump
existing.description_short: DOJ Fires 12+ Prosecutors Who Investigated Trump
existing.description_long: On January 27, 2025, acting Attorney General James McHenry signed termination letters for at least 12 senior Justice Department officials who had worked on special counsel Jack Smith's federal criminal investigations of Donald Trump. The letters stated explicitly that the officials could not be trusted to faithfully implement the President's agenda because of their significant role in prosecuting the president. Separately, approximately 40 prosecutors in the U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Columbia who had worked on January 6 cases were fired the same week. Acting U.S. Attorney Ed Martin simultaneously issued a memo launching a review of all January 6 prosecutions and declaring the use of the obstruction-of-an-official-proceeding statute a great failure. The DOJ also began compiling lists of FBI agents who had worked on Smith's investigations to identify candidates for termination. FBI Director Kash Patel subsequently carried out multiple purges of the bureau's senior ranks over the following months, forcing out field office leaders, senior agents, and attorneys connected to the two Trump criminal investigations. The fired prosecutors received no advance notice. Three FBI agents — Michelle Ball, Jamie Garman, and Blaire Toleman — later sued the administration in March 2025, alleging they were terminated in a retribution campaign for their work on the 2020 election investigation.

existing.description_short: Anti-Fauci Campaign - Attacking America's Top Doctor
existing.description_long: Donald Trump launched a vicious campaign against Dr. Anthony Fauci, the nation's top infectious disease expert, calling him a 'disaster' and claiming he had been around for '500 years' during a pandemic that killed over 400,000 Americans on Trump's watch. During a campaign call in October 2020, Trump attacked Fauci and other health officials as 'idiots,' declaring that 'people are tired of COVID' and tired of hearing from the nation's most trusted voice on the pandemic. Trump's attacks on Fauci intensified after the doctor appeared on '60 Minutes' saying he wasn't surprised Trump contracted COVID-19 after seeing him in crowded places with 'almost nobody wearing a mask.' The anti-Fauci campaign served multiple purposes: deflecting blame for Trump's failed pandemic response, appealing to his base's anti-science sentiment, and attacking expertise that contradicted his political messaging. Trump continued attacking Fauci long after leaving office, using him as a scapegoat for pandemic failures while promoting conspiracy theories about COVID origins and treatments. The systematic demonization of America's top infectious disease expert during a global health crisis represented an unprecedented presidential attack on scientific expertise and public health leadership. Fauci, who had served presidents of both parties for decades and was considered apolitical, became a lightning rod for Trump's culture war against science and expertise.

original_title: Family Separation Return - 'Zero Tolerance' Policy Reinstatement

existing.title: Family Separation Return - 'Zero Tolerance' Policy Reinstatement
existing.description_short: Family Separation Return - 'Zero Tolerance' Policy Reinstatement
existing.description_long: Donald Trump refused to rule out reinstating his family separation policy during the 2024 campaign and moved to revive elements of the practice after returning to office, despite the 'national uproar' it had created when thousands of children were separated from their parents at the southern border during his first presidency. Trump defended family separations as effective deterrents, claiming in November 2023 that 'when you hear you're going to be separated from your family, you don't come' and that 'it stopped people from coming by the hundreds of thousands.' His administration began terminating the Flores Settlement Agreement in May 2025, which had provided protections for migrant children in detention, while moving toward policies that would allow prolonged family detention and separation. Despite legal settlements requiring family reunification from his first term, indications emerged that family separation could return as Trump prioritized what he called deterrence over keeping families together. The administration's motion to terminate Flores claimed the agreement 'removes the disincentives enacted by Congress' and argued against protections that prevented long-term detention of children. While some former Trump officials expressed wariness about full reinstatement due to the previous 'national uproar,' Trump's continued defense of the policy and systematic dismantling of child protection agreements suggested family separations remained part of his immigration strategy.

original_title: Education Dept. Strips Transgender Student Protections Under Title IX

existing.title: Education Dept. Strips Transgender Student Protections Under Title IX
existing.description_short: Education Dept. Strips Transgender Student Protections Under Title IX
existing.description_long: On January 31, 2025, the U.S. Department of Education issued a Dear Colleague letter signed by Acting Assistant Secretary for Civil Rights Craig Trainor announcing that Title IX sex discrimination law would be enforced using the 2020 rules developed under Betsy DeVos during Trump's first term. The move eliminated the Biden administration's 2024 Title IX regulations, which had explicitly protected transgender students' rights to use bathrooms and locker rooms aligned with their gender identity and prohibited discrimination based on gender identity in federally funded schools. The guidance directed that all open Title IX investigations initiated under the 2024 rules should be immediately reoriented to comply with the 2020 framework, which treated sex as binary and provided no protections for gender identity. This followed Trump's first-day executive order declaring the U.S. recognizes only two sexes. Trainor specifically rejected the legal argument, based on the Supreme Court's Bostock decision, that Title IX's prohibition on sex discrimination extends to gender identity or sex stereotypes. The practical effect was immediate: transgender students at thousands of schools lost federal civil rights protections against harassment and discrimination. The guidance also raised questions about how the Education Department would handle sexual assault complaints, as the 2020 rules had been criticized for placing higher burdens of proof on assault survivors.

original_title: Trump Kills Biden EV Mandates and Guts CAFE Fuel Economy Standards

existing.title: Trump Kills Biden EV Mandates and Guts CAFE Fuel Economy Standards
existing.description_short: Trump Kills Biden EV Mandates and Guts CAFE Fuel Economy Standards
existing.description_long: On January 20, 2025, Trump signed an executive order revoking Biden's 2021 goal of 50% EV sales by 2030 and freezing $5 billion in unspent EV charging infrastructure funds, while directing EPA to reconsider emissions rules that would have required 30-56% EV sales by 2032. Then on December 3, 2025, the Trump administration proposed slashing the Corporate Average Fuel Economy standards from Biden's 50.4 miles-per-gallon fleet average target for 2031 down to 34.5 mpg — a 32% rollback that the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration's own analysis said would increase fuel consumption by roughly 100 billion gallons through 2050, costing Americans up to $185 billion more in gas expenses over that period. The White House called the CAFE reset delivering a win for American families, claiming it would lower car sticker prices by about $930. In June 2025, Trump signed a joint resolution ending California's authority to set its own stricter EV standards — effectively nullifying similar rules in 17 other states — and in July 2025 Congress zeroed out civil penalties for automakers that violate CAFE rules. Environmental and public health advocates warned the combined rollbacks would dramatically increase greenhouse gas emissions, deepen U.S. oil dependence, and set the domestic auto industry back by a decade compared to European and Chinese competitors.
